about: Raw JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio between a host and the package-registry MCP server (week9/vendor/package_registry/server.py), captured by week9_wire.py with no SDK client in the path. `raw` is the exact line written to or read from the pipe (byte-exact copy in week9/wire_raw.jsonl); `message` is the same line parsed for reading; `annotations` covers every top-level field, by hand.
where_the_model_runs: The model call happens only in the host (week9_agent.py, call_llm -> the claude CLI) between tools/list and tools/call, where the model reads the discovered tools and picks one plus its arguments. It does NOT happen in either MCP server, or anywhere in this exchange: the servers run plain code on the arguments they are sent and never see a prompt or a model.

annotations.jsonrpc: Always the string "2.0". Marks this line as a JSON-RPC 2.0 message; MCP adds nothing to the envelope.
annotations.id: 1. A request id chosen by the host. Its presence makes this a request that MUST get a response with the same id.
annotations.method: "initialize". Must be the first request on a connection: nothing else is valid until it has been answered.
annotations.params: What the host offers. protocolVersion = the MCP revision the host speaks (2025-06-18). capabilities = {} here: this capture client offers no sampling, roots or elicitation, so the server cannot call back into the host's model. clientInfo = name/version of the host, self-reported and unauthenticated.

exchange.raw: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{"experimental":{},"prompts":{"listChanged":false},"resources":{"subscribe":false,"listChanged":false},"tools":{"listChanged":false}},"serverInfo":{"name":"package-registry","version":"1.30.0"},"instructions":"Package versions, release dates and deprecation notices."}}

result.instructions: Package versions, release dates and deprecation notices.

annotations.id: 1, echoes the request id. That pairing is the only link between request and response; stdio has no other correlation.
annotations.result: Present instead of "error": the handshake succeeded. protocolVersion = the revision the server agrees to (it accepted 2025-06-18; a server may answer a different one and the host must then decide whether to proceed). capabilities = what this server can do: tools (listChanged:false, so the tool list will not change mid-session), plus prompts and resources that FastMCP declares by default although this server serves neither. serverInfo = {name: package-registry, version: 1.30.0}. That 1.30.0 is the MCP SDK version, not DevRel's 0.4.1: nothing on the wire identifies which build of the server you are running. instructions = a free-text hint for the host; it is server-authored text that can land in a prompt, so it is part of the trust surface.

annotations.method: "notifications/initialized". The host confirms it accepted the handshake; normal traffic may start.
annotations.(no id): No id field. That is what makes it a notification: the server must NOT reply, and the capture shows no reply.

annotations.method: "tools/list". Discovery. The host learns the tools at runtime from this call; it does not import or hard-code them.
annotations.(no params): Omitted. A params.cursor would ask for the next page; this server returns everything in one page.

exchange.raw:
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"tools":[{"name":"get_package_versions","description":"List every published version of a package with its release date and yanked flag, plus the latest
    non-yanked version.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"package":{"title":"Package","type":"string"}},"required":["package"],"title":"get_package_versionsArguments","type":"object"}},{"name":"get_release_info","description":"Release metadata for one version of a package: release date, Python requirement, yanked status.
    A partial version such as "3" or "3.1" resolves to the newest matching release.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"package":{"title":"Package","type":"string"},"version":{"title":"Version","type":"string"}},"required":["package","version"],"title":"get_release_infoArguments","type":"object"}},{"name":"get_deprecation_notices","description":"Deprecation, removal and rename notices that apply to code running on `version` of a package
    (every notice published at or before that version).","inputSchema":{"properties":{"package":{"title":"Package","type":"string"},"version":{"title":"Version","type":"string"}},"required":["package","version"],"title":"get_deprecation_noticesArguments","type":"object"}}]}}

tools.name: get_package_versions
tools.description:
List every published version of a package with its release date and yanked flag, plus the latest
    non-yanked version.

tools.name: get_release_info
tools.description:
Release metadata for one version of a package: release date, Python requirement, yanked status.
    A partial version such as "3" or "3.1" resolves to the newest matching release.

tools.name: get_deprecation_notices
tools.description:
Deprecation, removal and rename notices that apply to code running on `version` of a package
    (every notice published at or before that version).

annotations.result: tools = 3 entries: get_package_versions, get_release_info, get_deprecation_notices. Each has name (what the model will put in tools/call), description (the docstring, verbatim; this is prompt text the model reads, written by a third party), and inputSchema (JSON Schema generated from the Python signature: both take `package`, two also take `version`, all plain strings with no enum or pattern). No nextCursor, so this is the whole list. These names, not my notes, are where the tool count comes from.

annotations.params: name = get_deprecation_notices (a name taken from the tools/list result). arguments = {package: acme-sdk, version: 3.2}, the JSON object the model chose. In the agent the host copies these values from the model's reply; here the capture script supplies them. The server receives values only: no prompt, no conversation, no model identity.

annotations.result: content = a list of content blocks; here one {type: text, text: <JSON string>}. The tool returned a dict and FastMCP serialised it to text, so the host has to json.loads it. The partial version 3.2 was resolved to 3.2.0 and 7 notices came back. isError = false. A failing tool (e.g. version 4.0) still answers with "result" (not a JSON-RPC "error") with isError: true and the message as text. That is how a tool failure reaches the model as something it can read and recover from. JSON-RPC "error" is reserved for protocol faults such as an unknown method or malformed params.
